overview: Two states of chromatin packing that determine whether genes in that region are active or silenced.
genZNote: Euchromatin: open book, actively being read. Heterochromatin: book closed and shelved.

aspects.label: Transcriptional Activity
aspects.valueA: Transcriptionally active — genes here are being expressed.

aspects.label: Location in Nucleus
aspects.valueA: Found more centrally within the nucleus.
aspects.valueB: Often found at the nuclear periphery and around the nucleolus.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Regions containing actively used housekeeping genes.
aspects.valueB: Barr body (inactivated X chromosome) in female mammalian cells.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: The Barr body is a classic example of heterochromatin and is a favourite NEET/board question.
overlay.memoryTrick: Euchromatin = 'eu' (true/good) = active and open. Heterochromatin = tightly shut.
overlay.commonMisconception: Heterochromatin is not 'junk DNA' — it can contain genes that are simply switched off in that cell type.
